gaps.reason: source_id and consumer_id come from the certificate for update and model retrieval (met). Telemetry reports carry no identity field and the shared reporter credential is deliberately not individual, so nothing is bound there (kept).
Client certificates are checked by the service itself: a bearer token is ignored, and expired, not-yet-valid, wrong-usage and foreign-CA certificates are refused at the handshake.
Every model RPC except Health needs the consumer role; the private RPCs answer UNIMPLEMENTED on the public listener. GetModelPackage and StreamModelAsset are public by design (G8).
Model retrieval admits only registered installations (met). Telemetry accepts the one shared reporter credential, which avoids linkable reports and is revocable only as a whole (kept).
A revoked installation's new handshake fails after an atomic CRL swap, a corrupt CRL keeps the old configuration, and a deny-list entry takes effect on an open connection, all without a restart.

Plaintext is refused on every Compose-network listener (closed). Workstation loopback traffic between the supervisor, the worker and the bridge stays plaintext because it never leaves the host (kept; row X16).
The Go-era record: guarded-update and authentication rows against the Python services. This record repeats its authentication classes against the Rust stack.
The Rust-stack record. Its nine V3 rows that were not_run without the standard packages (T7, T9, T10, R8-wrong-pin, R8-not-allowlisted, I3, X1, X1b, X1c) are run here.

not_established: CK8, the positive controls and TL1-candidate run on their own Compose v3-training stack (param-update with its real gates over the pinned efficient release, and model-streaming), with the test PKI of the 13c-2 helper s13c_compose_pki (the privoke_pki crate), not the privoke-pki CLI PKI of the other rows. Their candidates are the 13c-2 export; no candidate was fitted here.
Application-level replay and tamper are the 13c rows C2a, C2b and C9, cross-referenced here, not repeated.

The store-unchanged half of TL1, TL2 and CK1 to CK7 is vacuous: their store is empty, so an admitted request and a refused one leave the same state. CK8 and TL1-candidate carry the check on a store that holds the pin and an admissible candidate.
The TL rows show that the TLS record layer refuses replayed and altered bytes; they say nothing about the supervisor's client admission (13c).
The client high-water mark is not observed: no client runs in this stack, and the version model-streaming serves stands in for it.
One run on one host (Windows 11, Docker Desktop, loopback); the rows are deterministic denials, not samples, and no repeat run was made.

static_evidence.claim: Every Rust server in the production and deployment Compose files starts with the five TLS flags (--cert, --key, --client-ca, --crl, --registry), passes no plaintext or insecure flag and sets no plaintext opt-out variable.
The only published ports are the two public listeners, 50443 and 58443, on loopback unless the operator overrides them.
No reverse proxy is referenced in any deployment path (G1).
Every deployed container has a read-only root, drops all capabilities, sets no-new-privileges and keeps Docker's default seccomp profile.
The cloud images are built with no cargo feature, so the workstation-loopback listener is never compiled in.
The model and telemetry servers still name their private RPCs, so the public/internal split that R9 and R10 exercise live is present in the source.
